explanations.projection: Projection systems display the movie on the screen. Modern cinemas use Laser (high brightness, long lifespan), LED (direct display, perfect blacks), or traditional lamp projectors.
explanations.projection-type: The technology used to project the image: Laser (35k-60k lumens), LED (1,200+ nits), Film (70mm legacy format).
explanations.brightness: Measured in lumens for projectors (higher = brighter) or nits for LED screens. Typical: Laser 35k-60k, LED 1,200+.
explanations.aspect-ratio: The width-to-height ratio of the screen. 1.90:1 (modern widescreen) or 2.39:1 (CinemaScope).
explanations.projection-brand: Major projector brands: Barco, Christie, Sony, NEC, RGB Laser. Each offers different quality and features.
explanations.sound: Audio systems deliver immersive sound. Dolby Atmos (3D audio with overhead speakers), Dolby Digital (traditional surround).
explanations.dolby-atmos: Immersive 3D audio with up to 128 audio tracks and overhead speakers. Creates a realistic sound environment.
explanations.dolby-digital: Traditional 5.1/7.1 surround sound. Good quality but lacks the overhead audio of Atmos.
explanations.digital-sound: Standard digital audio format. Basic but reliable surround sound experience.
explanations.analog-surround: Vintage 4.1 surround sound used in heritage cinemas. Nostalgic but limited compared to modern systems.
explanations.sound-channels: Number of audio channels: 5.1 (standard), 7.1 (enhanced), 11.1/7.1.4 (Atmos with overhead speakers).
explanations.seating: Number of seats available. Luxury cinemas offer recliners, premium legroom, and reserved seating.
explanations.screen-surface: The material that reflects light. Options include perforated (allows speakers behind screen), micro-perforated, or matte surfaces.
explanations.screen-material: Material types: Perforated (with tiny holes for speakers), Micro-perforated, Matte (smooth surface). Affects sound and image.
explanations.screen-gain: Reflectivity of the screen (1.2-1.8 typical). Higher gain = brighter but narrower viewing angle. Lower gain = wider viewing angle.
explanations.content-support: Types of content the theater can play: 3D (stereoscopic), HDR (high dynamic range), HFR (high frame rate), 4D (motion seats).
explanations.3d: Stereoscopic 3D using polarized or active glasses. Creates depth perception for immersive viewing.
explanations.hdr: High Dynamic Range - expanded brightness and color range. Standards: HDR10, HDR10+, Dolby Vision.
explanations.hfr: High Frame Rate - playback at 48fps, 60fps, or higher. Reduces motion blur, creates smoother motion.
explanations.4d: Motion seats with wind, water, scent effects synchronized with the movie for an immersive experience.
explanations.laser: Laser projection offers 35k-60k lumens brightness, better colors, longer lifespan (30,000+ hours), and instant on/off.
explanations.led: Direct LED display with 1,200+ nits brightness, perfect blacks (infinite contrast), no lamp replacements required.
explanations.70mm: Large format film stock offering superior image quality. Heritage format now mostly replaced by digital.
explanations.4k: Ultra HD with ~4,000 horizontal pixels. 4x the detail of 1080p. Sharper, more lifelike images.
explanations.2k: HD with ~2,000 horizontal pixels. Standard cinema resolution. Good quality but less detailed than 4K.
explanations.film: Traditional film projection using celluloid. Offers unique look but requires film projectors and film stock.
explanations.resolution: Image detail: 2K (HD), 4K (Ultra HD), 70mm (large format). Higher resolution = sharper images.
